newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Japan's share of steam coal declining-ABARE.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Japan's share of steam coal declining-ABARE.

text.p: Japan's share of total Asian steaming coal imports are projected to fall to fall dramatically as more coal is shifted to newly idustrialised and developing regions of of Asia, including Taiwan, Thailand and the Philippines, the Australian Bureau of Agricutural and Resource Economics (ABARE) forecast on Thursday.
By 2010, Japan's share will have fallen to about a third of total steaming coal imports compared with about half currently, ABARE said.
Total imports of steaming coal by all regions of Asia are forecast to rise 200 percent over the same period.
The shift is the result of the rapid growth in the demand for coal in Asia, due largely to increasing electricity generation.

"While some countries in the region, notably China and Indonesia, will meet their increased demand for coal from domestic production, most will seek their supplies from the international market," ABARE said.
However, the strongest growth in global energy consumption is expected to be in natural gas, Guy Caruso of the Paris-based International Agency, told an ABARE seminar on energy.
"The fastest rate of growth in gas consumption will occur in Asia and electricity generation will be continue to be one of the major users of gas," Caruso said.

Mark Levine of the Lawrence Berkely National Laboratory told the seminar China has become the second largest energy consumer as well as the fastest growing source of greenhouse emissions in the world, despite making strides in its energy programmes since the 1970s.

"Without these improvements, China's already massive energy consumption would be twice its actual level and China would contribute not 13 percent but 25 percent of global carbon emissions," Levine said.
